column2: The Grand Debate
As a distinguished leader of [From.Society.GetName], [From.GetTitledFirstName] called its members to a Grand Debate before the eyes of Verena.

I expect many members of [Root.Society.GetName] to come to the Grand Debate, and everything must be flawless. The preparations are well underway: my steward has seen to the lodgings, the cooks have stocked the larders and the great hall has been hung with the owl and scales of Verena. All that is left is to send out the invitations.
Bring me my most trusted courier!

A courier has arrived with a letter sealed in the owl of Verena. [From.GetTitledFirstName] bids every member of [From.Society.GetName] to a Grand Debate at [From.GetHerHis] court, where the learned of the Old World will test their wits before the Goddess of Wisdom.
A splendid chance to show what I know!
A foolish waste of time.

The guests are arriving as I speak. For the next few weeks each of them will put their learning on display before Verena and before their peers, and when it is over we shall know who is the wisest among us.
Let the debate begin!
I have been named the winner of the Grand Debate! Nobody else argued half so well, and nobody else knew half so much. Verena's priests have written my name in the great book of the cult.
The sweetest of all sounds is praise.
Many distinguished themselves during the debates. None, however, did as well as [From.GetTitledFirstName], who has been named the winner of the Grand Debate!
Well done!
Congratulations are in order.

After weeks of long arguments and longer nights, the Grand Debate is over. There were a few heated words, and one chair thrown, but I think most of those who came would agree that Verena was well served.
A most successful gathering!
Those who attended will think §G5§! better of you for five years.\n
I may not have won the Grand Debate, but I have gained a great deal all the same. The arguments taught me new ways to put my learning to use, and even how to improve upon it.
The last guests have left, and the halls are quiet again. Thinking back on my own part in the debate, I see that it taught me new ways to put my learning to use.
A triumph in my eyes.
The Grand Debate is over and I did not win. Still, a few of my arguments drew loud applause, and people will remember them.
The last guests have left, and the halls are quiet again. Thinking back on my own part in the debate, a few of my arguments drew loud applause, and people will remember them.
A noteworthy success.
The Grand Debate is over, and although I did not win, I learned a few things by watching the others.
The last guests have left, and the halls are quiet again. Thinking back on the debate, I learned a few things by watching my guests.
A worthwhile effort.
The Grand Debate is over and I did not win. I cannot say I learned anything either. Study and preparation will be the key next time.
The last guests have left, and the halls are quiet again. Thinking back on the debate, I see how much I still have to learn. I must prepare better next time.
It was still time well spent.
The Grand Debate is over and I achieved nothing at all. My opponents outwitted me at every turn, and I was laughed at for my efforts.
The last guests have left, and the halls are quiet again. Thinking back on the debate, I achieved nothing at all. My own guests outwitted me at every turn and laughed at me under my own roof.
A shameful display...
You improve your chances of winning the debate.\n
You lessen your chances of winning the debate.\n

Late in the evening, talking with a fellow member of [Root.Society.GetName], I find myself discussing the power of a well-turned phrase. When I joke that I ought to deliver my arguments in verse, [fellow_debater_target.GetTitledFirstName] nods, to my surprise. "Do not underestimate a good rhyme," [fellow_debater_target.GetSheHe] says. "The old bards of Sigmar's tribes won more feuds with verse than with axes."
Perhaps it is exactly what my argument needs!
The rest of your evening is spent on the finer points of poetry.\n
Nonsense! I will keep to facts, not ornaments.

During today's debate I am unsettled to find my rival [rival_debater_target.GetTitledFirstName] watching me. I take a deep breath and carry on with my reasoning. When I am done, I am startled to see [rival_debater_target.GetFirstName] on [rival_debater_target.GetHerHis] feet, smiling. With a raised eyebrow [rival_debater_target.GetSheHe] gives me a nod of respect.
I am glad we can see past our differences at times like these.

After hours of listening to scholars of very varied wit, I admit my thoughts sometimes drift... Yet one person keeps drawing me back. [striking_debater_target.GetTitledName] has a mind and a way with words unlike any I have met.

After hours of listening to scholars of very varied wit, I admit my thoughts sometimes drift... It should not surprise me that one person keeps drawing me back. [striking_debater_target.GetTitledFirstName] has always had a way with words, and a presence that is hard to ignore.
I... I am not sure what these feelings are!

While we argue [Root.GetDebateSubject], I am struck by the urge to tell a joke a stable-hand once told me. It would make my point perfectly. And even if it does not, laughter might win me just as many friends.
So a Halfling walks into a temple of Verena...
The joke may fall flat, but if it lands you could charm the beards off the dwarfs in the room!
This is no time for foolish tales.
You sit back down.

...and if those words, spoken by a simple Halfling, do not prove my point, nothing ever will.\nI am not sure anyone heard my conclusion over the roars of laughter, but it hardly matters. The whole room is mine.
As witty as I am wise!

I stand before the room in utter silence for a full minute before asking again: "Get it?"\nSomeone drops the stylus they were using to sketch the Eight Winds of Magic. The small clatter sounds as loud as a temple bell.
I can never show my face to these people again!

I hear [fellow_member_1.GetTitledFirstName] before I even enter the room. "[fellow_member_2.GetTitledFirstName], you clearly know nothing of [Root.GetDebateSubject]! Why are we even having this conversation?"
[fellow_member_1.GetFirstName], there you are! Keep your voice down, would you?
[fellow_member_2.GetFirstName], what is [fellow_member_1.GetSheHe] going on about?
I am sure this is all a misunderstanding.
I should pretend I was never here...

[fellow_member_target.GetTitledFirstName] has spent the whole morning lecturing everyone on [Root.GetDebateSubject], and has not once let anyone else finish a sentence. A small prank with a few of my reagents slipped into [fellow_member_target.GetHerHis] wine would take [fellow_member_target.GetHerHim] down a peg. It would cost me the reagents, and if anyone saw, my own good name as well.
It would be worth it.
You spoil the chances of §Y[fellow_member_target.GetTitledName]§! making a good impression at the Grand Debate.\n
No. I respect my fellow scholars.
However pompous they are.\n

These past days I have felt a restless energy rising in me, begging to be used. "I could start a new treatise! No, wait, I should prepare my notes for tomorrow," I mutter. My eye falls on a stack of blank parchment, and it occurs to me that I could write to my dear [inspired_letter_target.GetTitledFirstName].
Words cannot truly say how I love [inspired_letter_target.GetHerHim], but I will try.
Warm words, to show how much I value [inspired_letter_target.GetHerHim].
I will make it hard for [inspired_letter_target.GetHerHim] not to like me.
My dear [inspired_letter_target.GetFirstName]... I would not be who I am without you.\nIn the end the floor is littered with drafts, and you spend all night perfecting the letter.\n
I have long meant to put my feelings into verse.
A small poem, to show how much I value [inspired_letter_target.GetHerHim].
Even [inspired_letter_target.GetSheHe] cannot resist a good poem.
I would not be who I am, were it not for you. You are my Mannslieb and my Morrslieb, my dawn and my dusk.\nIn the end the floor is littered with drafts, and you spend all night perfecting the poem.\n
Focus! The debate is what matters now.

A long and heartfelt letter has come from [From.GetTitledFirstName], who is away at the Grand Debate of the Cult of Verena. It is full of fine words about how much I mean to [From.GetHerHim], written with an earnestness I have seldom seen in [From.GetHerHim] before. I wonder what brought this on...
[From.GetFirstName] must truly care for me.

Many of my fellow debaters stay up late, honing their arguments far into the night, and so have I. The lack of sleep is telling on me. My mind wanders, I catch myself staring into nothing, and as I leaf through my notes for points nobody has yet made, my hands tremble.
This is too important to stop now.
I just want to rest. I do not care who wins.
A draught from my own reagents will see me through.
You use up one of your ingredients.\n

The Grand Debate is wearing me down. I have not slept well since I came. Either my back aches on these wretched beds, or I am woken by loud arguments in the corridor about yesterday's subjects. On nights like these I long for my own warm bed.
These lodgings are the worst...
I cannot bear it any more. I am going home!
I should put these sleepless nights to use.

A chance has come to level the field. [sabotage_target.GetTitledFirstName] is a fine debater, but [sabotage_target.GetSheHe] leans heavily on [sabotage_target.GetHerHis] meticulous notes, and [sabotage_target.GetSheHe] leaves them lying about.
Perhaps [sabotage_target.GetSheHe] could find a few of mine...
Leave forged notes about a ground-breaking discovery where they will be found.\n
It would be a shame if anything happened to those notes.
Try to make the notes unreadable.\n
I will not stoop to cheap tricks.

After a long day of debating I find myself alone in a corridor, and spot some notes forgotten on the floor. They deal with [Root.GetDebateSubject]! Splendid. I could use these to prepare for my next debate.

After a long day of debating I find myself alone in a corridor, and spot some notes forgotten on the floor. They deal with [Root.GetDebateSillySubject]! Splendid. I could use these to prepare for my next debate.
Even someone else's learning is a path to success.
You will recite this new-found knowledge in an upcoming debate as if it were your own.\n
I have more faith in my own work.
This is clearly made-up nonsense!
As I sit studying my notes for today, [From.GetTitledFirstName] stumbles and drops everything [From.GetSheHe] was carrying. Parchments and quills fly everywhere, and my notes are soaked in ink!
An unfortunate accident.
[From.GetFirstName] did that on purpose!
Your notes for today are ruined, lessening your chances of winning the debate.\n
I managed to "accidentally" spill ink over the notes of [From.GetTitledFirstName], ruining them past reading. [From.GetFirstName], however, is far from pleased with my clumsiness...
You cannot bake a pie without breaking a few eggs.
I did splendidly in today's debate, thanks in no small part to the brilliant research I found in the corridor. My opponents had nothing to set against my flawless logic.

Reciting the notes I found the other day was a grave mistake... The crowd was loud and lively, not because my brilliance struck them, but because they were laughing. Someone must have written those notes as a joke!
In today's debate I recited the notes I found far too closely... Before long someone in the audience was on their feet, shouting that I was a fraud who had stolen their work.
With a little luck, anything is possible.
Everyone present was impressed, improving your chances of winning the debate.\n
I was a fool to trust those notes!
This is embarrassing...
This embarrassment will not soon be forgotten, and lessens your chances of winning the debate.\n
Clearly there is some mistake. Let us all calm down!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] made a fool of [From.GetHerselfHimself] at the debate today by quoting the forged notes I planted for [From.GetHerHim] to find. At times [From.GetSheHe] had the whole hall in tears of laughter!
For all my efforts, [From.GetTitledFirstName] ignored the notes I left in plain sight.
[From.GetSheHeCap] certainly is gullible...
I will fool [From.GetHerHim] next time!
the true nature of the Eight Winds of Magic
whether Verena's justice binds even the gods
the lost libraries of Nehekhara
the reckoning of the Imperial Calendar
the vanished Old Ones and their works
the proper weighing of evidence at a trial
the histories of Sigmar's tribes
the meaning of the twin-tailed comet
what the Elves truly took with them when they left the Old World
whether the dead may be questioned without offending Morr
the healthful properties of a little warpstone in one's porridge
proof that the Halflings were the Old Ones' chosen people
a goblin who was taught to read, and then to write sonnets
Ranald's lost recipe for an ale that makes the drinker invisible
the secret third moon that only the drunk can see
the domestication of the squig as a lapdog for ladies of the court
